summary: The plan is self-sufficient and correct against the pinned ref. I re-measured every quantitative claim directly from the 13 packaged products.parquet artifacts (53 rows, 13 providers, 12 distinct product_ids, 21 distinct descriptive tuples, per-provider counts 2..9) and every literal in section 5, and all of them match the plan exactly. I reconstructed the write-set independently with git grep and found the same six tracked paths the plan declares, with no omission: __init__.py only re-exports the symbol, and every other `products()` occurrence is a provider-handle or provider-module call the plan explicitly fences off. The returned shape is a built-in list[str], never CatalogResult or pl.DataFrame; the unscoped result is the sorted twelve-id vocabulary; provider scoping is the same shape restricted to that provider's packaged rows; an unknown provider raises UnknownProviderError with the exact message the source produces (registry.py:44). product_info and _global_products are explicitly held unchanged, so the milestone-9-owned alias is untouched. Every affected existing assertion in test_discovery.py, both catalogue-only files, test_m2_exit_criteria.py and test_m5_exit_criteria.py is enumerated and either rewritten or proven untouched, and the reader-delegation call count {stations:1, products:2} still holds under the new implementation. The typecheck fixture tests/typecheck/nominal_window_misuse.py is neither touched nor is the gate widened, the gate order and lockfile rules are stated verbatim, and the reversibility constraints (no version bump, no tag, no push, untracked pr-body.md, one conventional commit) are all respected. The only residue is a self-healing lint consequence the plan does not call out: deleting both m5 tests orphans `import rivretrieve as rr`, which `uv run ruff check --fix` removes automatically without reddening a gate.
